Starting a business in China,
in the right order.

Five decisions come before the first yuan of capital: whether you need an entity at all, whether you are allowed to do this, which vehicle, how money moves, and who keeps it legal. Most foreign founders start at the fourth.

The five decisions

  1. 01 Does your business need a Chinese entity at all? Fit
  2. 02 Are you allowed to do this, here? Access
  3. 03 Which vehicle, and who controls it? Structure
  4. 04 How much capital, and how does money move? Money
  5. 05 Who runs it, and how does it stay legal? Continuity

Read top to bottom. A "no" at any layer ends the plan — that is the point of doing them in order.

Why this exists

The information is not missing. The order is.

English-language advice on starting a company in China is abundant and almost entirely about the mechanics of registration. The decisions that determine whether registration is a good idea are made earlier, and nobody sequences them.

01 — Access first

The list decides, then the licence

A sector can be open to 100% foreign ownership and still be impossible to enter because the licence is not issued to new companies, or because the premises cannot meet the standard. The negative list is the first gate, not the only one.

02 — Structure second

A vehicle is not a strategy

A WFOE, a joint venture and a representative office do different things. Founders choose by tax rate, then discover the vehicle cannot hold the licence they need. Control and permission come before optimisation.

03 — Verification

Paths, not conclusions

We do not tell you a city is easy. We tell you which counter to stand at, which documents to ask for, and what a written answer looks like — because registration practice is municipal and changes without much notice.

Read in order

The five layers

01

Does your business need a Chinese entity at all?

Most founders register a company before they can say what the company is for. Start with the job the entity has to do — invoice, hire, hold a licence, or nothing yet.

Fit 02

Are you allowed to do this, here?

The negative list, the sector licence and the registered address decide whether a company is possible at all — before structure, capital or tax matter.

Access 03

Which vehicle, and who controls it?

WFOE, joint venture, representative office or a Hong Kong holding company: four different answers to control, liability, tax and the exit you will need one day.

Structure 04

How much capital, and how does money move?

Registered capital is a promise with a five-year clock. The bank account, the capital account and the invoice system decide whether you can actually trade.

Money 05

Who runs it, and how does it stay legal?

Work permits, payroll, social insurance, annual filings, audit and the closure you will eventually need. A company is a recurring obligation, not a one-off filing.
